newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday May 22.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* The government won its 23rd lower house confidence vote gaining approval for a decree aimed at speeding up the process for starting or resuming state construction projects (all).

* The upper house Senate approved the creation of a watchdog authority for the communications sector after the separatist Northern League decided to withdraw most of the 3,000-odd amendments it had presented to snarl the bill's progress (all).
* The cabinet will hold a meeting today to start discussing reforms to the welfare state. (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi said the privatisation of Italian state-controlled telecoms holding STET was proceeding at full speed and according to the government's programme (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Preliminary figures released by another seven sample cities confirmed Italian consumer price inflation rose 1.5 percent year-on-year in May, raising expectations for a cut in the official discount rate (all).
* Alberto Zuliani, chairman of the national statistics institute ISTAT, said favourable conditions existed for Italy's cost of living to maintain its current lower trend.
* Stock market watchdog Consob approves the prospectus for the flotation of a third tranche of shares in energy giant ENI. (all).

* Jean De Jaegher, managing director of clothing and textiles group Marzotto, said the company expected turnover in 1997 to increase four to five percent. De Jaegher also said the group's profits in the first quarter of 1997 rose 24 percent to 29.4 billion lire (all)

* Information technology group Olivetti said it had sold its whole stake in office equipment company Olivetti Synthesis to a group of enterpreneurs that would manage the business through Siccma SpA (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Shareholders of Banco di Sicilia elected Gustavo Visentini as the southern Italian bank's new chairman (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
